reason: VALUE/TRANSFER lens. (1) The per-event arithmetic checks out, but the ceiling is below the gate. Un-forking an evaluable FP fork changes J from TP/D to TP/(D-1). At J_pub 0.36 (CONTEXT.md l.1320, +-0.04) that is +0.0004..+0.0016 score per FP for G = 20-60. Un-forking a TP gives D unchanged and J - 1/D, i.e. -0.0017..-0.005 per TP. In closed form, removing a fraction k of the FP forks at zero TP loss gives 0.1*(1/(1/J - k(1/P-1)) - J), which depends only on the public fork precision P and not on the counts. With P 0.53-0.65 and k 0.25 this is +0.0018..+0.0031. (2) k on the public embryo is smaller than the local 14/43 = 33%. (a) The rule is restricted to safe-division forks. On the idea's own base (x138 + insertion) part of the evaluable FP forks are exempt DaughterNet forks; locally that is 21 of 64 FP (v2 feasibility verify), so the effective k is k_sd x 0.7-0.9. (b) The local k_sd is in-sample and rests on one embryo: 10 of 11 mid>=4 FPs come from 6bba, and 44b6 has only 1 of 10 at mid>=4 and 3 of 10 with the cos arm (v2 transfer verify). The 44b6 events may also be duplicates of one physical event, because 44b6 clips are overlapping crops of one recording. (c) The proposed 4.5 um threshold removes 6/43 FP (14%), not 11-14. The cos>=0.1 arm has a margin of only 0.1 over the TP max of 0.00 (about 6 degrees). With 0.5-0.7 um of out-of-sample position noise on 4-5 um arms (angle noise about 6-9 degrees per arm), the cos arm carries most of the TP-loss risk. GT divisions have cos p90 +0.03 (r1_research l. GT pass). (3) Monte Carlo over the unknowns (G 20-60, J 0.36+-0.02, public precision 0.45-0.75, safe-div share of FP 0.7-0.9, k_sd 0.10-0.30, per-TP-fork loss 0.5-4%): public gain mean +0.0008, median +0.0009, p10 -0.0014, p90 +0.0030. P(>= +0.002) = 0.23 and P(< 0) = 0.20. On average about 2.3 FP are removed and 0.37 TP lost. That is below the +0.002 bar and well inside LB noise (0.003). As a rider in a bundle it can never be attributed, which the idea itself admits. (4) The transfer checks it passes: nodes are untouched (no node-multiplier artefact), and it does not trust network confidence. The side rule uses edge_prob == 0.0 only as an 'unscored' flag. (5) The validation protocol is weaker than claimed. Its 'out of sample' re-check on idea 1's x138 train tails is out of sample only in the stack, not in the data: the detector, edge net and V1284 head were all trained on these same train videos. The thresholds were read off the same 199 videos. A pass on 5 (44b6) + 18 (6bba) TP forks bounds the per-TP loss rate only at ~12% (95%). Idea 1 (divins-x138-lab-retune) was itself refuted by its value verifier, so that cache may never be built. The rider would then ship on exp39-derived evidence alone, measured on a different coordinate stack: head shift mean 0.74 um, max 1.61 um, against a 0.24 um margin at 4.0 and 0.74 um at 4.5.
fix_if_any: Nothing makes it reach +0.002 public; the zero-loss ceiling is about +0.0027 at the best plausible k. The best repair for a free rider: (a) mid >= 4.5 um only, and drop the cos>=0.1 arm unless the x138 train cache shows TP cos max <= -0.15. (b) Safe-division forks only (NaN prob and not div_inserted), run as the very last edit. (c) Smart side rule (drop the ILP-side edge only when its prob == 0.0). (d) FORKMID_ENABLE=0 byte-identity test. (e) Ship only inside a bundle that is justified without it, and pre-register that no LB delta is attributed to it. If idea 1's x138 train cache exists, require 0 TP forks removed and a TP-mid margin >= 0.7 um on that cache; otherwise keep 4.5 um. Private EV is roughly the same small positive number with about a 20% chance of being negative; it is a coin-flip-plus rider, not a lever toward 0.99.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0008 expected (median +0.0009; p10 -0.0014, p90 +0.0030; P(>= +0.002) ~0.23, P(< 0) ~0.20); about +0.0005..+0.0009 for the 4.5 um-only variant. Invisible under LB noise 0.003.
realistic_private_gain: +0.0003..+0.0008 expected over the unseen private embryos (the sign depends on whether they look like 6bba (k ~0.2-0.3) or 44b6 (k ~0.1); P(< 0) ~0.2, driven by out-of-sample TP-fork position noise, mainly on the cos arm).
